key_insight: Treat the corruption level (masking/noise ratio) as a controllable, continuous degree of freedom and learn a Flow-Guided Neural Operator (FGNO) that maps corrupted time-series to clean signals, yielding more flexible and effective self-supervised representations than fixed-mask MAEs.
problem_solved: Standard masked autoencoders use a fixed, predetermined masking ratio, which can be suboptimal for diverse temporal scales, noise conditions, and downstream tasks; this paper addresses the lack of adaptability in corruption modeling for SSL on time-series data.
method: Introduce FGNO: a neural operator architecture guided by learned flow fields that conditions reconstruction on a continuous corruption parameter (masking/noise level).
Train with a spectrum of corruption levels so the model learns a mapping across the corruption continuum, enabling interpolation and extrapolation between corruption settings.
Integrate FGNO into a self-supervised reconstruction objective for time-series, producing robust, adaptable representations without hand-tuning a single masking ratio.
impact: FGNO reduces the need to tune a single masking ratio, improves robustness across varying temporal dynamics and noise levels, and offers practitioners a more flexible pretraining paradigm that transfers better to diverse time-series tasks.
visual_elements: Schematic: input time-series + corruption-level control → Flow-Guided Neural Operator → reconstructed output (annotate conditioning signal).
Continuum diagram: varying masking/noise ratios along a slider showing interpolation of learned reconstructions.
Comparison bar/line graphic: static-mask MAE vs FGNO across multiple downstream tasks (robustness/transferability) — qualitative labels rather than exact numbers.
Flow field illustration: stylized vector/flow overlay on time-series to convey how FGNO models temporal transformations across corruption levels.
paper_title: Self-Supervised Learning via Flow-Guided Neural Operator on Time-Series Data
paper_authors: Duy Nguyen, Jiachen Yao, Jiayun Wang, Julius Berner, Animashree Anandkumar
